# Requirements Document: Order retention

## Introduction

IATA Resolution 797 asks the airline that owns an order to keep it accessible
for 13 months from its creation and from its first usage while an item is
open, and for 7 days once every item has reached a final status.  It does not
say how 13 months is counted on UTC instants, so the model takes the count as
a parameter.

These requirements are generated from the Lean model in [`Rules/OneOrder/Creation/Retention.lean`](https://github.com/samdengler/verified-air/blob/main/Rules/OneOrder/Creation/Retention.lean). Each acceptance criterion carries the status the build computed for it: *proven* means a theorem the build checked, *example only* means a computed example, *open* means a theorem the build could not prove, and *not checked* means no theorem or example covers it yet.

## Requirements

### Requirement ONE-406

**User Story:** As a seller, I want an order to stay retrievable while the customer can still use it, so that I can service the trip and any value it holds.

**Rule:** THE SYSTEM SHALL keep an order accessible for 13 months from its creation and for 13 months from its first usage while it has an active item, and for 7 days after every item has reached a final status. (Lean: `mustKeep`)

#### Acceptance Criteria

1. WHILE an order has an active item THE SYSTEM SHALL keep the order accessible until 13 months after its creation.
   - ONE-406.1, proven: proven theorem `keep_from_creation`; example `retentionOfPaidOrder`
2. WHILE an order has an active item and has been used THE SYSTEM SHALL keep the order accessible until 13 months after its first usage.
   - ONE-406.2, proven: proven theorem `keep_from_first_use`; example `retentionOfPaidOrder`
3. WHEN every item of an order has become closed or cancelled THE SYSTEM SHALL keep the order accessible for 7 more days.
   - ONE-406.3, proven: proven theorem `keep_after_final`; example `deliveredOrderRetention`
4. WHILE an order has an active item THE SYSTEM SHALL keep the order accessible.
   - ONE-406.4, open: open theorem `keep_while_active`; counterexample `storedValueNeverUsed`

#### Open question on ONE-406.4

> An order is kept while it has an active item, under every reading and
> every count of months.
>
> Open question for the business.  The resolution asks for 13 months from
> creation and 13 months from first usage, and nothing after both have passed.
> An item whose services are removed with their value held stays active for as
> long as the customer does not use the value.  The example
> `storedValueNeverUsed` shows it: two years after creation the order still
> holds value and no longer has to be kept.  What are an open item and first
> usage, and must an order that still holds value stay accessible?
